gates.text: Open a Frame / Fan out / Cross-judge / Pick / Graft / Verify checklist before launching. Freeze the task, artifact, grounding and permitted changes. Derive 3–6 concrete gradeable rubric criteria; candidates see the same task, not the picker’s rubric.

Resolve `arena runners` with pstack_route and use its emitted native sessions_spawn arguments for both independent candidates, launched concurrently within authorized resource limits. Give each a separate writable worktree or task-owned output directory, shared grounding paths, and instructions to produce the artifact plus a short rationale naming considered/rejected alternatives. Preserve exact native role selections; no guessed model-family fallbacks or provider installation. Missing delegation is BLOCKED, not a sequential bakeoff.

Collect all candidate runs through their accepted native completion path before judging. A candidate with no usable output is a recorded dropout; proceed with the remaining artifacts, never count a queued or still-writing candidate as complete. Read full artifact files, not truncated result summaries.

AFTER candidate writing has stopped, resolve `arena cross-judge pool` through pstack_route and spawn ONE independent read-only native sessions_spawn judge using its emitted selection. The judge sees the rubric and each candidate’s artifact path under an exact label: with the workflow ledger, the slot id its spawn plan lists (such as `candidates:0`); otherwise a label the parent assigns and later passes to pstack_brief check. It scores every criterion under those labels and recommends a base with rationale. Require a verified different family from the current parent, selecting the first eligible entry in configured pool order. Inherited or same-family entries never judge. Missing current-parent/family metadata or an eligible judge leaves the gate BLOCKED; never infer family from a model ID, substitute a default or skip judgment to claim completion. The tool path qualifies current-turn metadata; native-command admission remains a separate unresolved capability decision, not evidence that this gate ran. A missing or failed judge leaves the cross-judge gate BLOCKED and prevents a completed arena verdict.

The lead reads EVERY candidate end to end, scores each criterion independently and records those scores under each candidate's exact label before any judge score is visible to it; the native controller enforces this with its `lead` checkpoint, spawning the judge only after the lead's scores are recorded. Collect the judge, compare verdicts and read both rationales before resolving disagreement; agreement is evidence, not a substitute for the lead’s inspection. Pick the base easiest for a future maintainer to extend without breaking invariants, preferring a cleaner boundary or smaller API on ties. Resolve judgment/prose routing before any delegated synthesis.

Walk every losing candidate again for coherent improvements, normally one or two per candidate; adapt by hand under one mental model, never paste a majority of every candidate together. Convergence needs no forced graft. Wild divergence means an underspecified frame: reframe and rerun rather than averaging incompatible shapes.

Verify the synthesized real artifact and affected behavior. If verification exposes a bad frame, reframe/rerun; if a candidate caught the missed issue, return to Graft. Do not paper over it. Return one artifact and a synthesis note naming base/why, judge verdict and disagreements, each graft/source, rejections/why, convergence, dropouts, diversity limitations and verification/blockers.

For long routed phases, spawn announcing children (without `collect`; a collector is collected in the turn that spawned it) and use a short bounded native wait, then hand off pending run IDs and finish on resume under [the shared lifecycle](contract.md#collection-and-resume); never respawn accepted children or claim pending work complete.

8. Candidates return the `arena-runner` [output contract](agent-briefs.md#panel-output-contracts), without rubric scores, and the judge returns `cross-judge`, scoring exactly the usable candidates on every criterion. An invalid output stays pending for a corrected object from the same child; it is never rewritten by the parent.
